title: Routing and Internet Architecture
description: How packets find a path across independently owned networks: prefixes, IGPs, BGP, peering, and the failures that are political.

sourceReferences.title: Stanford CS144
sourceReferences.notes: Internet architecture after a working transport. BGP is policy, not a shortest-path toy.

sourceReferences.title: A Border Gateway Protocol 4 (BGP-4)
sourceReferences.notes: Path-vector reachability plus attributes. Policy, not shortest path.

sourceReferences.title: Domain Names — Concepts and Facilities
sourceReferences.notes: Hierarchy, resolvers, and caches as a system.

modules.title: Forwarding
learningObjectives: Separate the datapath lookup from the process that filled the table
Let the more specific prefix win

modules.title: Inside an AS
learningObjectives: Treat an AS as one routing policy
Flood a map inside the AS, then run shortest path

modules.title: Between ASes
learningObjectives: Route between ASes by policy, not shortest path
Name hijacks and leaks as failures of that policy

modules.title: The system around it
learningObjectives: Treat DNS, anycast, and CDNs as systems that ride the routing plane
Measure and fail in ways that are political as well as technical

concepts.name: Forwarding versus routing
concepts.summary: The lookup in the datapath versus the process that filled the table.
objectives: Distinguish forwarding (the datapath lookup) from routing (the process that filled the table)
Predict what still works if the routing process dies but the forwarding table remains

concepts.name: Longest-prefix match
concepts.summary: More specific wins.
objectives: Explain longest-prefix match as the more specific prefix winning
Apply two overlapping prefixes to decide which next hop a destination takes

concepts.name: Autonomous systems
concepts.summary: A network with one routing policy.
objectives: Describe an autonomous system as a network with one routing policy
Predict why two networks that share a cable still need a protocol if they have different policies

concepts.name: Interior gateway protocols
concepts.summary: How an AS talks to itself.
objectives: Explain an IGP as how an AS computes paths inside itself
Distinguish an interior protocol from the protocol used between ASes

concepts.name: Link-state routing (OSPF)
concepts.summary: Everyone floods the map, then runs shortest path.
objectives: Describe link-state routing as flooding a map and then running shortest path
Predict what each router recomputes after a link-state advertisement arrives

concepts.name: BGP
concepts.summary: Policy routing between autonomous systems.
objectives: Explain BGP as policy routing between autonomous systems, not shortest path
Predict why a longer AS path can still be chosen when policy prefers it

concepts.name: Peering
concepts.summary: Settlement-free exchange, until it is not.
objectives: Describe peering as settlement-free exchange of customer routes
Predict why a peer will not typically offer transit to the rest of the Internet

concepts.name: Transit
concepts.summary: Paying someone to reach the rest of the Internet.
objectives: Describe transit as paying another AS to reach the rest of the Internet
Contrast a transit link with a settlement-free peer

concepts.name: Internet exchange points
concepts.summary: A room where many ASes meet.
objectives: Describe an IXP as a fabric where many ASes meet to peer
Predict why an exchange reduces the need to buy transit for some paths

concepts.name: Policy in the path
concepts.summary: Local preference and AS-path as politics encoded in attributes.
objectives: Explain local preference and AS-path as policy encoded in attributes
Predict which attribute typically decides a route before AS-path length does

concepts.name: Route hijacks
concepts.summary: Announcing a prefix you do not own.
objectives: Describe a route hijack as announcing a prefix you do not own
Predict why a more-specific unauthorized prefix can steal traffic

concepts.name: RPKI
concepts.summary: Cryptographic permission to announce a prefix.
objectives: Explain RPKI as cryptographic permission for an AS to originate a prefix
Predict what origin validation does and does not stop

concepts.name: The DNS as a system
concepts.summary: Hierarchy, caches, and the resolvers in the middle.
objectives: Describe the DNS as a hierarchy of zones, caches, and resolvers
Trace a name from a stub resolver through caches to an authoritative server

concepts.name: Anycast
concepts.summary: One address, many locations, routing decides which.
objectives: Explain anycast as one address announced from many places, with routing choosing
Predict why two clients can reach different locations for the same address

concepts.name: Anycast DNS
concepts.summary: Why 8.8.8.8 is near everyone.
objectives: Explain anycast DNS as putting the same resolver address near many clients
Predict why 8.8.8.8 can be a short hop from almost anywhere

concepts.name: CDNs
concepts.summary: Putting the bytes next to the viewer.
objectives: Describe a CDN as putting bytes next to the viewer using DNS and/or anycast
Predict why a cache miss at the edge still has to fetch from an origin

concepts.name: IPv6
concepts.summary: Larger addresses and a different neighbor-discovery story.
objectives: Describe IPv6 as larger addresses and a neighbor-discovery story instead of ARP
Predict what a host uses to find a neighbor's link address on IPv6

concepts.name: MPLS
concepts.summary: Labels instead of IP lookups in the core.
objectives: Explain MPLS as forwarding on labels instead of repeating an IP lookup in the core
Predict what a core router looks at when a labeled packet arrives

concepts.name: Software-defined control
concepts.summary: A logically centralized controller filling the tables.
objectives: Describe SDN as a logically centralized controller filling forwarding tables
Contrast a distributed control plane with a controller that computes paths

concepts.name: Measuring the Internet
concepts.summary: Traceroute lies, and we use it anyway.
objectives: Explain why traceroute can lie and why we still use it
Predict a case where ICMP replies do not reveal the true forwarding path

concepts.name: Anycast at L7
concepts.summary: When the TCP connection and the HTTP cache disagree about where you are.
objectives: Explain the clash when a TCP connection and an HTTP cache disagree about where the client is
Predict what breaks if routing moves an anycast TCP flow to a different site mid-connection

concepts.name: BGP and anycast interaction
concepts.summary: A more-specific prefix pulling traffic across an ocean.
objectives: Explain how a more-specific prefix can pull anycast traffic across an ocean
Predict why policy and prefix length can override nearest for an anycast address
